characters: Ananse: a charming, expressive folkloric spider character walking upright with a round brown body, clever bright eyes, and a small woven kente sash.
Nyame: the majestic, kindly Akan Sky God with a silver beard and golden kente robes, seated among glowing golden clouds.
Aso: Ananse’s wise, warm-hearted wife wearing a colourful headscarf and wrapper inside their cosy earthen home.

narrationPlan.voice: A lively storyteller; a booming voice for Nyame and a quick, clever voice for Ananse
narrationPlan.pace: Lively storytelling, with a pause for each task (about 85 words per minute)
notes: Read dialogue with a different voice for each character.
Pause for two seconds at each question activity.
Never rush the last page: let the ending land.

music: A bright drum and a quick xylophone for Ananse (placeholder)
culturalNotes: In the most common version told, Nyame sets four tasks: to bring Onini the python, the Mmoboro hornets, Osebo the leopard, and Mmoatia the fairy. Versions differ: some leave out Aso, and some name three tasks instead of four. This telling follows the common version and notes that tellings vary.
Anansesem means “spider stories”. Ananse tales are Akan tales told across Ghana and the diaspora.
The story reminds children plainly never to approach or trap wild animals.

teacherGuide.overview: A retelling of the Akan tale of how Ananse won the world’s stories, noting that versions differ and reminding children never to trap wild animals. It teaches sequencing, folktale features, teamwork, and respect for oral tradition.
learningGoals: Retell the four tasks in order.
Describe one way that versions of the same tale can differ.
beforeReading: Ask children what Ananse tales they already know.
whileReading: Hold up four fingers as each task is named on page 2.
afterReading: Act out the story in four short scenes.
Ask an elder or parent for their version of the tale and compare.
discussion: Why does the story say two minds are better than one?
How can two storytellers tell the same tale differently?
reflection: Who do you ask for help when a task feels too big?

support: Use four picture cards for the four tasks.
stretch: Write what you think Aso whispered to Ananse as part of their clever plan.
